resourceName: Rewetting of the Paltinskoye Peatland for Climate Resilience in Perm Krai
description:
The Rewetting of the Paltinskoye Peatland project is a large-scale ecological restoration initiative aimed at mitigating climate change by restoring degraded peatlands in Perm Krai, Russia. Peatlands are among the most efficient carbon sinks on Earth, yet when drained, they become significant sources of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, releasing CO₂, methane (CH₄), and nitrous oxide (N₂O). This project addresses these challenges by rewetting 212 hectares of the Paltinskoye peatland in Phase I, preventing further peat degradation, reducing fire risks, and restoring natural carbon sequestration processes. 
By restoring the peatland’s natural hydrology, this project is estimated to sequester 112,522 tCO₂e over a 40-year period (2026–2065) in Phase I. Beyond carbon benefits, the project contributes to biodiversity conservation, enhances ecosystem services such as water filtration and flood control, and supports local communities through job creation and education on sustainable land management.
